calamity.evidence: J. C. Connor’s substantive Calamity! reference, Imagine 12 March 1984, printed 14 / PDF 16, actually retrieved in an unchanged clear 54-page original scan from a public Internet Archive collection. Full original review page visually read; fresh 300 dpi left/middle-column OCR checked and right-column operative continuation/earthquake paragraph manually transcribed. Selective complete gameplay paragraphs exclude unrelated Monster Manual review, opinion and money-supply complaint. Accurate rules_reference_pdf, not the full physical Games Workshop 1983 manual. Matches named insurance game BGG1542; no ID change. Gives 2–6 players as insurers, 52 weeks/13 per quarter, premiums paid to surviving policy owners only at circuit end, two circuits and most-cash win; £1,500,000 start, movement cards 1–5 with one circuit per pack and first-year redeal; four policy risk levels, optional £20,000 offload before row die and £100,000 after row before column die, £200,000 claims per affected policy, and earthquake affecting all types without offload. The reviewer’s presumably qualification remains explicit. Complete deck allocation, all board-space effects, bankruptcy/loan timing and full ending exceptions remain missing. Two unchanged supporting components preserve archive metadata and matching original gallery. Retrieved PDF MD5/SHA1 match archive metadata; stable archive.org URL redirects to recorded download host. Earlier distinct 53-page spawningpool scan rendered this review unreadably in the current reader and was not accepted; separate public OCR corroborates but is not substituted for checked original text. Specific MAJOR for reversed insurer cash flows, dice movement and one-circuit ending in local summary. No full summary audit, complete playable set, PASS or summary body repair.

calamity.specific_finding: The summary teaches dice movement, an ending after one circuit, and insurance policies that pay the player compensation for losses while charging ongoing premiums. Connor’s contemporary reference (Imagine 12, March 1984, printed 14 / PDF 16) instead makes players the insurers: they receive premiums on policies still in force at year-end and pay £200,000 per policy hit by the two-die risk grid. Movement uses cards numbered 1–5, and the game lasts two circuits, with most cash winning. Reversing the insurance cash flows and replacing both movement and ending changes central procedures. Specific MAJOR for those covered rules only; full manual, all board effects and bankruptcy/loan exceptions remain missing. No full audit or summary body repair.
